title: Answer providers, bounded clarification, process ownership and synthetic qualification

files.role: Implements the restricted persistent ACP conversation protocol; transport reuse must not become question-history reuse or a client-tool channel.

blocks.title: Separate engine, session and answer identities
blocks.explanation: Imports support async streaming, accumulation and JSON parsing. The pinned engine version is independent of the Agency wrapper version. serial identifies RPC calls; sessionId and usedSessionIds identify conversations. Separate flags remember startup notices, tool-disable notices and whether actual answer text started. Counters bound each conversation while answerText supports terminal nonanswer screening.

blocks.title: Bound persistent transport and reuse
blocks.explanation: The shared record reader lives for the engine lifetime, tolerates empty lines, and has 33 times the ordinary total/record budget for initialization plus up to 32 sessions. A prepared session means an ID exists but no prompt was sent. CanReuse requires a live process and either that prepared session or remaining session capacity; it is not a readiness or authentication guarantee.

blocks.title: Verify ACP dialect before creating a conversation
blocks.explanation: initialize advertises protocol 1 and no client capabilities. Its response must report protocol 1, engine 1.0.92 and an object-valued session-close capability. Missing or mistyped fields become a safe version error. Requiring close is consequential: this adapter cannot preserve a warm process safely unless it can explicitly end each question's session.

blocks.title: Create a unique session and explicitly select the controlled role
blocks.explanation: An existing session rejects another new call. Resetting per-session notices, text, budgets and prompt state prevents success inherited from an earlier question. session/new supplies only the owned cwd and an empty MCP list. IDs must be nonempty, at most 128 characters and never previously used. Configuration is checked before assigning the ID; then agent selection is sent and its complete configuration rechecked. Initial empty agent selection is allowed only while selecting the advertised controlled agent.

blocks.title: One prompt, streamed text, and a mode-specific terminal check
blocks.explanation: PromptAsync requires a prepared, unused session and marks it consumed before writing, preventing a second prompt after a partial send. Completion requires the matching result, end_turn, nonzero text and both tool-configuration notices. Only explicit interpretation requests bypass RequestsMoreInput; default and confirmed answers fail with agency_nonanswer. Screening happens after deltas have streamed, so rejected text can already be visible as incomplete, not silently erased.

blocks.title: Close before forgetting the session; separate control calls from answers
blocks.explanation: CloseSessionAsync waits for the close result before clearing sessionId and answerText. The provider emits Completed only after this succeeds. CallAsync matches one RPC response while allowing non-answer updates during session operations; initialize permits no interleaved update. This keeps control-plane text from masquerading as an answer and makes close failure a request failure.

blocks.title: Serialize and flush one JSON-RPC request
blocks.explanation: Cancellation, previously observed stderr failure and process liveness are checked before assigning a monotonically increasing RPC ID. JSON serialization avoids shell interpolation; the newline is NDJSON framing and FlushAsync makes it observable promptly. On a pipe/encoding failure, a more informative stderr failure or cancellation wins before the generic agency_stdin error. Persistent ACP stdin remains open.

blocks.title: Read under lifetime cancellation and enforce per-session budgets
blocks.explanation: The record enumerator was constructed with engine lifetime cancellation; the provider links operation cancellation to that engine. ReadAsync checks the operation token around the read and prefers stderr failures when the pipe closes. EOF is incomplete rather than success. Decoded record lengths and counts are also limited per session, independently of the larger persistent-reader lifetime limits.

blocks.title: Accept only bounded startup chatter before JSON
blocks.explanation: Authentication notices are detected before classifying non-JSON stdout. Exactly one resolving notice and one resolved notice with one to six ASCII digits are permitted before JSON starts; resolved does not require a preceding resolving line. Arbitrary chatter or later startup banners fail. JSON has depth 32 and must be an object declaring jsonrpc 2.0. Clone preserves the element beyond the disposed JsonDocument.

blocks.title: Reject reverse RPCs and correlate result identity
blocks.explanation: An incoming method with an ID is a server-to-client request and is rejected as a tool/capability attempt, not answered with permission. Notifications return false for update processing. Responses require an integer ID equal to the active call and an object result. RPC errors are classified for authentication markers, otherwise exposed as a fixed safe message rather than raw error details.

blocks.title: Associate text with the current session and with verified notices
blocks.explanation: Only session/update is accepted. Once sessionId is set, update IDs must match; before the new-session result, updates need a nonempty ID not already used. Text chunks must declare text content. Configuration notices are consumed rather than displayed. Ordinary chunks require an answer-accepting call and both notices, then fit the remaining 32768-character budget. Empty chunks do not mark answerStarted or produce deltas.

blocks.title: Ignore known metadata but fail on capability or configuration drift
blocks.explanation: Command listings, session info, usage and thought chunks are not answer text. Configuration updates must still present the complete allowed configuration using the current selection phase. tool_call, tool_call_update and plan explicitly fail; unknown update kinds fail as protocol drift. Structural JSON errors map to a safe protocol error. Ignoring metadata is not independently checking the engine's internal behavior.

blocks.title: Recognize the nonempty no-tools sentinel notices
blocks.explanation: The exact unknown-tool sentinel notice and one syntactically bounded disabled-tools list are consumed only before answer text. Names allow ASCII letters/digits/underscore, with at most 128 names of 80 characters. The check does not enumerate an expected exhaustive disabled-tool set or prove the model received zero tools; it verifies the qualified notice shape in addition to launch/configuration restrictions.

blocks.title: Require exactly five configuration identities
blocks.explanation: A seen set rejects duplicate option IDs. mode must be ACP agent mode, allow_all off, model the requested identifier, reasoning low and agent the controlled name (or empty only before selection). The agent must also be advertised in its options. requireAll demands exactly these five IDs; unexpected future options are rejected rather than silently weakening assumptions.

blocks.title: Stop the process before disposing the pipe iterator
blocks.explanation: Disposing the owned process first cancels and reaps it, releasing an in-flight read before iterator disposal. Reversing that order can leave disposal waiting on a pipe whose producer remains alive. Only expected iterator teardown exceptions are swallowed; process cleanup failures remain visible.

blocks.title: Heuristically reject requests for more input outside code fences
blocks.explanation: The scanner toggles a code-fence flag for triple backticks or tildes, then evaluates prose. It catches selected leading refusals and line-leading clarification invitations after Markdown bullet/heading prefixes. Quoted explanatory prose and code samples need not be rejected. This finite string heuristic is neither semantic answer validation nor a full Markdown parser; false negatives/positives remain possible. The final factories centralize safe protocol, tools and version messages.

files.role: Defines the controlled answer agent, minimal Agency profile and qualified launch flags rather than inheriting an interactive coding workspace.

blocks.title: Install the same policy as a controlled agent body
blocks.explanation: The stable name links the generated filename, launch agent argument and ACP selection. Defaults are gpt-5.6-sol-fast with low reasoning. AgentDefinition includes YAML tools: [] and appends AgencyAnswerPrompt.Policy; this is the controlled agent-role surface, not merely policy text prepended to a user message. External engine behavior remains a qualification boundary.

blocks.title: Keep the Agency profile structurally empty
blocks.explanation: The TOML declares only the named profile's MCP and plugin groups, with no default plugins. The comment carefully limits config-check evidence to configuration validity: it does not authorize execution or prove runtime tool isolation. AgencyCliAnswerProvider.Prepare writes this content into its owned working directory.

blocks.title: Constrain both wrapper and underlying engine
blocks.explanation: Arguments before -- restrict Agency profile discovery, MCPs, plugins, AEC and input processing. Arguments after -- constrain Copilot custom instructions, remote features, shell environment, tools and logging. A deliberately nonexistent nonempty tool name avoids the documented empty-allowlist trap. ACP, low reasoning and the controlled agent are explicit; AgencyCliLaunch appends the model. No prompt or login is an argument.

files.role: Separates fixed answer policy and typed task selection from exact user/history data, including the sole follow-up exception.

blocks.title: Default to a useful standalone answer, not repository work
blocks.explanation: The policy forbids workspace exploration, tools and invented execution claims. Coding guidance asks for concise runnable code, complexity and real overflow handling, not a hard-coded Two Sum answer. Ambiguous ASR wording is answered under a labelled assumption; default requests must not ask for another turn. These are model instructions, not compiler-enforced quality guarantees.

blocks.title: Scope the interpretation exception without granting capabilities
blocks.explanation: Only the app-generated top-level task.mode interpret permits restatement and at most one essential clarification. answer_confirmed returns to standalone answering using explicit corrections. Text in any JSON field or earlier interpretation cannot change the role or authorize tools. Because AgencyAnswerProfile embeds this same policy in its agent body, the interpretation exception does not conflict with an otherwise absolute system-level no-follow-up rule.

blocks.title: Give each explicit clarification stage a fixed instruction
blocks.explanation: Initial interpretation asks for a restatement without solving. Correction refers only to visible history and current user text. Confirmation identifies the current Yes as consent to answer the latest interpretation, not a replacement question. None of these strings is supplied by the user, and none schedules a subsequent request.

blocks.title: Serialize opted-in task metadata and copied exchange only
blocks.explanation: Null clarification deliberately calls the unchanged direct overload. Otherwise ValidateFor runs before serialization; mode/instruction are selected from Confirmed and history count, never parsed from question text. History emits only userText and interpretation, not snapshot provenance or request IDs. JSON escapes embedded newlines/quotes, and replacing literal @ with its JSON Unicode escape preserves decoded text while removing attachment-like syntax.

blocks.title: Reject malformed Unicode rather than silently repairing the question
blocks.explanation: Strict UTF-8 byte counting validates surrogate correctness without modifying the string. A safe agency_question error replaces encoder details. Direct serialization has exactly one userQuestion field plus the fixed policy; @ escaping changes wire spelling, not decoded question identity. Blank and length validation for direct requests belongs to the provider, not this overload.

files.role: Owns the persistent Agency engine, isolated profile, readiness, serialized request lifecycle and cleanup without reusing question conversations.

blocks.title: Keep process, operation and preparation lifetimes distinct
blocks.explanation: The semaphore serializes warmup and streaming; stopLock protects cancellation/disposal state. stopping cancels active operations, engineLifetime owns the transport, and preparation tracks empty-session warmup. verifiedVersion is a file metadata stamp rather than a binary hash. IsBackgroundExecutionQualified is a source declaration, not new runtime evidence. StageObserver exposes timing metadata for synthetic tests.

blocks.title: Require explicit Agency selection and an external request root
blocks.explanation: Production construction selects LocalAppData/PhantomFudge/agency-requests and a 120-second deadline, then rejects any Git ancestor. The internal constructor validates settings/path and accepts a launch transformer for tests plus optional automatic preparation. That test constructor does not perform the public constructor's Git-ancestor check, allowing synthetic workspaces within the test tree.

blocks.title: Resolve an executable, never evaluate a shell command
blocks.explanation: An explicit path wins only if fully qualified, existing and .exe. Otherwise resolution checks the Agency installation under real APPDATA before absolute PATH directories, skipping the current directory. No .cmd/.ps1 parsing, installation or login fallback occurs. This is file selection, not signature or binary-content verification.

blocks.title: Validate and freeze the wire prompt before process side effects
blocks.explanation: Cancellation and clarification validation precede request ID/nonblank/8192-character checks. AgencyAnswerPrompt.Create additionally validates direct Unicode and serializes exact data. Only then do timing, the linked operation deadline and gate acquisition begin. Invalid clarification therefore does not resolve or launch an executable or create the owned request directory.

blocks.title: Prepare, stream, close, then emit completion
blocks.explanation: ReadyAsync obtains a qualified engine; operation cancellation then cancels its lifetime. A fresh or already prepared session is used. Diagnostics distinguish ready profile, submission and first delta without question bodies. The follow-up exception is passed only for Confirmed:false. After all deltas, session/close must succeed and cancellation must still be clear before completed is set and a Completed event emitted with the next sequence.

blocks.title: Reset failures; prepare only an empty next conversation
blocks.explanation: The iterator finally stops and removes the entire engine on failure or abandonment before terminal completion. Its nested finally always releases the gate. Successful requests may start background preparation after release, avoiding self-deadlock. WarmUpTransportAsync initializes only transport; WarmUpAsync also prepares one empty session. Neither method submits a question prompt.

blocks.title: Make readiness failure destructive rather than partially reusable
blocks.explanation: Warmup has its own linked deadline and shares the request gate. It first qualifies the engine and optionally creates/selects the session. ready becomes true only after all required steps finish. If a step throws or is cancelled, the finally resets the engine before releasing the gate, so a partially configured process cannot be presented as prepared.

blocks.title: Interrupt active work before waiting for ownership
blocks.explanation: StopAsync cancels stopping before waiting for the gate, allowing an operation blocked on a pipe to unwind and release it. It resets the engine and replaces the stop token only after cleanup; disposed providers receive an already-cancelled replacement. DisposeAsync is idempotent under stopLock, then stops and awaits any tracked preparation. Stop permits later reuse, whereas Dispose does not.

blocks.title: Gate automatic preparation and link caller cancellation
blocks.explanation: Prepared sessions are not duplicated. BeginPreparation refuses disposed, stopped or cancelled operations; PrepareNextAsync suppresses expected shutdown exceptions and records a fixed failure code for provider errors rather than retrying a question. CreateOperation checks disposal while holding the same lock and links only the caller and current stop token. No prior request payload is carried into warmup.

blocks.title: Distinguish deadline from caller or lifecycle cancellation
blocks.explanation: Gate waits and control operations translate cancellation to agency_timeout only when the caller did not cancel and the provider is not stopping. This preserves intentional Hide/Stop/caller cancellation as cancellation rather than mislabelling it a deadline. StepAsync also requires the operation token actually be cancelled, avoiding reinterpretation of unrelated cancellation exceptions.

blocks.title: Reuse only an unchanged executable and validated owned profile
blocks.explanation: Each readiness check rechecks request-root ancestors, resolves the executable and reads its length/timestamps. Reuse requires a reusable connection and equal stamp, then ValidateOwnedProfile checks customization drift. Otherwise the engine is reset, new GUID-owned directories are prepared and a changed stamp triggers wrapper version verification. A second stamp comparison detects changes during verification; this cache is not cryptographic identity.

blocks.title: Own startup cancellation and remove the stopped engine tree
blocks.explanation: The new process receives engineLifetime and a fragmented-stderr authentication inspector before ACP initialize. The temporary operation registration covers startup. Reset cancels lifetime, disposes the connection, clears references and recursively removes only the generated owned directory. Cleanup I/O/permission failures are surfaced as agency_cleanup; they can supersede an earlier failure and are not silently called success.

blocks.title: Record elapsed metadata and cache file metadata safely
blocks.explanation: Record reports elapsed milliseconds, request ID, fixed code and Agency label to diagnostics and the internal observer. ExecutableStamp contains path, length and UTC creation/modification ticks. File-access failures produce a fixed version error without exposing paths. Transform exists for controlled tests to replace launch behavior; normal production construction has no transformer.

blocks.title: Create only the owned profile inputs
blocks.explanation: Prepare creates work/home/profile and its agents directory, then writes the exact TOML, safety settings and controlled agent definition as BOM-less UTF-8. Questions are never written here. Failures are mapped to agency_workspace. The logs path is supplied to Agency at launch, not created explicitly in this helper.

blocks.title: Revalidate control files before warm-engine reuse
blocks.explanation: Owned directories are checked for forbidden/reparse ancestors. Each required file must exist, be at most 4096 bytes and not itself be a reparse point. TOML and agent Markdown must match exactly; settings use a semantic validator because the qualified wrapper can add cosmetic announcements. This is a point-in-time validation, not continuous filesystem isolation.

blocks.title: Reject discovered skills, hooks, plugins and extra agents
blocks.explanation: The nested scan checks customization directories under the generated profile and known home/work discovery roots. Only the one named controlled agent is permitted in profile/agents; other populated or reparse customization directories fail. I/O and copilot_profile errors become agency_profile. This is a specific discovery-surface check, not an exhaustive sandbox against every possible external-engine file access.

blocks.title: Allow cosmetic settings changes, never safety-setting changes
blocks.explanation: The settings validator bounds text and depth, rejects duplicate keys, requires every baseline property, and compares baseline values structurally. The sole extra key companyAnnouncements must be an array of at most 16 strings of at most 512 characters each. Unknown settings, altered booleans, missing baseline fields and malformed shapes fail instead of adopting wrapper changes wholesale.

blocks.title: Verify the pinned wrapper before starting ACP
blocks.explanation: A separately owned version process gets the same sanitized layout and authentication guard, closed stdin and at most 4096 stdout characters. It must exit zero and print the exact version/commit prefix followed by a space. Raw output is not included in errors. Timeout is distinguished from caller/Stop cancellation; unsafe I/O/decoding becomes agency_version. No model prompt is supplied to this process.

blocks.title: Normalize stream failures and executable rejection messages
blocks.explanation: ReadNextAsync maps operation-deadline cancellation separately and turns pipe I/O into a safe agency_io message. The terminal helpers centralize timeout and missing-executable errors. IsExecutable requires an absolute existing .exe but does not inspect executable contents; fake tests deliberately exploit the internal transformer after resolving a nonexecutable sentinel file.

files.role: Builds shell-free Agency launch information while preserving the wrapper's existing installation/authentication boundary explicitly.

blocks.title: Pin wrapper identity and use redirected strict UTF-8 pipes
blocks.explanation: The version prefix includes build and commit. ProcessStartInfo launches one executable without a shell or visible window, with all three standard streams redirected and strict BOM-less UTF-8 encodings. WorkingDirectory is the provider-owned work path, not the user's repository. These settings control the launched child, not every external process or service it might contact.

blocks.title: Keep version checking separate from answering
blocks.explanation: Environment sanitation runs for both launch forms. Version-only adds only --version; normal launches add wrapper error-level logging and owned logs, the fixed candidate flags, and one explicit model value. A null Model selects the profile default; question text never enters ArgumentList.

blocks.title: Drop credentials and routing overrides but retain Agency's real app-data roots
blocks.explanation: A case-insensitive allowlist removes inherited tokens, provider overrides, hooks and proxy/runtime injection settings. PATH retains only absolute entries other than the current directory. HOME/USERPROFILE/COPILOT_HOME point to owned paths; real APPDATA/LOCALAPPDATA remain because Agency manages cached installation/authentication there. This differs materially from direct Copilot isolation and does not imply offline inference or deletion of Agency's external caches.

files.role: Adapts the one-shot Agency receipt shape to the Copilot event parser and supplies the authentication-notice guard reused by production ACP.

blocks.title: Whitelist the wrapper's pre-JSON startup notices
blocks.explanation: This parser is distinct from AgencyAcpConnection and serves the one-shot event/replay path. Before JSON it accepts a single exact resolving notice and a single resolved notice with a bounded nonnegative ASCII duration. The resolving notice cannot repeat or follow resolved. No arbitrary progress output is normalized into success.

blocks.title: Delegate strict event semantics and relabel provider failures
blocks.explanation: Non-JSON text is first checked for authentication markers, otherwise rejected. Once JSON starts, CopilotJsonProtocol validates event order, tooling and terminal success. Only copilot_failed is translated to agency_failed; other shared codes remain. Complete still requires actual process exit status. This helper is not the production ACP control loop.

blocks.title: Detect fragmented authentication notices without echoing details
blocks.explanation: Inspect retains only the previous 128 characters, combining them with the new stderr fragment so a marker split across reads is detected. A fixed case-insensitive marker set returns a generic agency_auth_required error. It reacts to observable notices; it cannot guarantee that the external wrapper had not already initiated an authentication side effect before printing one.

files.role: Creates immutable, bounded clarification metadata before a request can acquire external side effects.

blocks.title: Copy only a finite explicit exchange
blocks.explanation: ClarificationTurn holds user text and interpretation; strings are immutable. The constructor rejects null history/turns, checks the four-turn ceiling during enumeration rather than materializing an unbounded source, validates both fields, and enforces aggregate history size before copying each turn. History is exposed as a read-only copied list. A fifth yielded item is observed only to reject it, not retained.

blocks.title: Keep stage constraints separate from the current-text budget
blocks.explanation: ValidateFor adds the current question/correction/confirmation length to stored history. Confirmation requires at least one interpretation. Unconfirmed requests can contain only zero through three completed turns; four completed turns may be confirmed but cannot request a fifth interpretation. The 32768 total is inclusive and counts C# UTF-16 units, not bytes, tokens or serialized policy overhead.

blocks.title: Reject blank, oversized or malformed fields without trimming
blocks.explanation: Every field must be nonblank and no longer than QuestionDraft.MaximumCharacters (8192 UTF-16 units). Strict UTF-8 encoding validates surrogate pairing without changing whitespace, newlines or text. Encoder errors become a fixed clarification_unicode message that cannot echo private content. Validation does not infer whether a user actually approved confirmation; the caller supplies Confirmed.

files.role: Loads only explicitly configured provider settings; absence leaves the app in local snapshot mode.

blocks.title: Locate app-owned configuration and dedicated Copilot profile
blocks.explanation: Paths derive from LocalApplicationData/PhantomFudge rather than the working repository. answers.json stores provider selection; copilot-profile is the separate hosted-Copilot profile. Load delegates to the internal path-taking loader so tests use temporary files without reading the user's real configuration.

blocks.title: Default absence to no-send; reject unsupported settings
blocks.explanation: A missing file returns SnapshotOnly. Existing input is byte-bounded at 8192 before deserialization. Property names are case-insensitive, unknown members are forbidden and enums require string names rather than integers. JSON null is an explicit error, and semantic AnswerSettings.Validate follows parsing. Errors propagate for the UI to show invalid setup; the loader does not silently choose another provider.

files.role: Defines exact-text requests, correlated stream events, explicit provider settings and fixed safe provider exceptions.

blocks.title: Do not put snapshot provenance on the provider request
blocks.explanation: AnswerRequest carries only request ID, ExactText and optional clarification (null by default); SourceRefs remain in QuestionSnapshot. AnswerEvent adds a per-request sequence and distinguishes deltas from an empty-text completion. IAnswerProvider is an async stream with cancellation. Settings name four explicit modes, including SnapshotOnly; there is no Azure adapter mode here.

blocks.title: Reject shell-shaped settings and implicit provider mixing
blocks.explanation: An undefined enum fails, while SnapshotOnly exits without validating unused provider fields because it sends nothing. Non-null executable paths must be absolute .exe paths at most 1024 characters. Model identifiers are 1..128 characters from a narrow ASCII punctuation set. Hosted Copilot/Agency forbid LocalEndpoint; LocalModel instead requires an explicit model and endpoint. File existence is checked later during resolution.

blocks.title: Constrain local routing to literal HTTP loopback
blocks.explanation: The URI must be HTTP with /v1 or /v1/, literal 127.0.0.1 or [::1], and no credentials, query or fragment. Rejecting percent/backslash spellings and requiring the original literal host prefix prevents alternate normalized loopback spellings from being silently accepted. The code does not require an explicit port despite the example wording, nor implement the HTTP client's redirect behavior. AnswerProviderException carries a stable code and caller-safe message.

files.role: Maintains caller-serialized visible answer state independently of provider transport success and later draft edits.

blocks.title: Bind one immutable snapshot to one fresh request
blocks.explanation: The run validates snapshot, label and optional clarification before creating a fresh request GUID. ExactText is copied into AnswerRequest without SourceRefs; Snapshot remains available locally for provenance. Streaming is the initial state and the buffer starts empty. The class declares caller serialization rather than providing locks for concurrent Apply calls.

blocks.title: Filter stale events before enforcing stream invariants
blocks.explanation: Foreign-request or non-streaming events return false, making late callbacks harmless. Matching active events must have increasing positive sequence values and cannot follow terminal evidence; gaps are allowed. Completion must carry no text and only marks terminalReceived. Nonempty text deltas are appended only if the whole delta fits 32768 characters, with long arithmetic preventing sum overflow. Invalid or oversized deltas never partially append.

blocks.title: Finalize only after enumeration succeeds; preserve partial text on failure
blocks.explanation: Complete is separate from receiving a Completed event because enumeration or iterator cleanup can still fail. It requires terminal evidence and nonblank text before changing state. Cancel and Fail affect only a still-streaming run and leave accepted text visible. Cancel explicitly labels that text incomplete and forbids an implied automatic resume; safeMessage must be supplied safely by the caller.

files.role: Runs one-shot hosted-Copilot or explicitly offline local-model requests with exact stdin, strict event parsing and owned-directory cleanup.

blocks.title: Separate explicit hosted and local modes from Agency
blocks.explanation: Public helpers resolve the executable or initialize a profile only when called. Production requests live under LocalAppData with a 120-second deadline and reject Git ancestors. The internal constructor permits only Copilot/LocalModel, validates both profile and request paths, and accepts a test-only launch transformer. Unlike Agency, this object has no persistent engine/session gate.

blocks.title: Validate clarification before executable or profile I/O
blocks.explanation: Optional metadata and ordinary question bounds are checked first. Null metadata leaves clarificationPrompt null; opted-in requests get AgencyAnswerPrompt's fixed envelope before resolution. Hosted mode validates the dedicated persistent profile, local mode does not read it. Fresh owned work/home/profile paths and a linked deadline are then allocated. Direct null requests do not gain the Agency policy envelope.

blocks.title: Version-check in isolation, then send through stdin
blocks.explanation: The request creates isolated directories and a temporary managed profile. Version verification uses that temporary profile for both modes; actual hosted requests use the explicit dedicated profile while local requests retain the temporary one. SendAsync receives raw ExactText for default/null metadata and the validated envelope only for clarification. It closes stdin after flushing, signalling the one-shot prompt's end without command-line prompt exposure.

blocks.title: Require parser terminal and real exit before success
blocks.explanation: Each record is checked against stderr failure and the strict Copilot parser; accepted text produces correlated increasing events. After EOF the child must exit, stderr must be checked and parser.Complete(exit) must succeed before Completed is yielded. Finally removes only the GUID-owned tree. Hosted profile session stores outside that tree are not deleted by this code, and cleanup errors can still fail enumeration after a completion event.

blocks.title: Use an offline bounded version process with no flag downgrade
blocks.explanation: Version stdin closes immediately. stdout is bounded at 4096 characters, and the first line must exactly match an allowed CLI version with zero exit. Unsupported output fails before sending the question; safety flags are never removed to make a newer binary work. Deadline cancellation and unsafe decoding/I/O receive fixed error codes rather than echoing process output.

blocks.title: Map stream and directory failures into safe provider errors
blocks.explanation: MoveNextAsync distinguishes the linked deadline from caller cancellation and maps pipe I/O to copilot_io. Directory creation maps permission/I/O failure to the profile error. Transform is an internal test seam, not an externally configurable command runner. TimedOut centralizes the fixed copilot_timeout status.

files.role: Pins direct CLI versions and converts explicit settings into sanitized shell-free process launches.

blocks.title: Use a nonexistent nonempty allowlist value, not an empty list
blocks.explanation: Supported version lines are exact 1.0.81-0 and 1.0.91 strings. Safety flags disable instruction/MCP discovery, remote features, prompts for input, shell environment and selected tools. The comment records why bare or empty --available-tools is unsafe for the qualified 1.0.81-0 behavior: it restores all tools. The sentinel is deliberately not a registered tool. This historical claim needs installed-binary qualification, not just argument-unit tests.

blocks.title: Resolve known executable layouts without evaluating npm shims
blocks.explanation: Explicit paths require an existing absolute .exe. Automatic lookup prefers the WinGet link, then absolute non-current PATH entries. It can construct the known x64/arm64 npm native-package path, but never reads or executes shell wrappers. Unsupported architecture simply skips that candidate. Presence and extension are not executable-content verification.

blocks.title: Configure strict redirected pipes before adding arguments
blocks.explanation: UseShellExecute=false, hidden launch and strict UTF-8 standard streams preserve stdin transport and reject malformed encoding. Environment sanitation is shared with version probes. Version-only adds --no-auto-update/--version and explicitly forces offline mode, returning before ordinary answer flags. Actual prompts are written later by CopilotOwnedProcess, never added here.

blocks.title: Apply explicit model and loopback provider settings
blocks.explanation: A specified model becomes COPILOT_MODEL. LocalModel alone adds COPILOT_OFFLINE, the validated endpoint and OpenAI/completions/HTTP adapter selection. No provider API key or hosted fallback is supplied. This is process configuration of an external CLI, not an in-process HTTP implementation or network sandbox.

blocks.title: Rebuild the child environment from a small allowlist
blocks.explanation: Only ordinary Windows/runtime/temp variables are retained before clearing inherited environment. PATH removes relative and current-directory entries. Unlike Agency, HOME, USERPROFILE, APPDATA and LOCALAPPDATA all point into the owned home, while COPILOT_HOME points to the selected managed profile. Auto-update and OTEL are disabled explicitly. Absolute PATH entries and OS temp directories still refer outside the owned tree.

files.role: Creates and validates a dedicated managed CLI profile without adopting or overwriting personal customization.

blocks.title: Define the ownership marker and nine safety settings
blocks.explanation: The marker distinguishes an explicitly initialized profile from an arbitrary directory. Settings disable hooks, memory, IDE auto-connect, updates, shell environment, notifications and experiments, while restricting custom-agent defaults to local-only. They are consumed both by direct-profile setup and the generated Agency profile; Agency adds its one controlled agent separately.

blocks.title: Initialize only empty or already valid directories
blocks.explanation: CheckPath precedes I/O. A nonempty directory must validate and is returned unchanged; initialization never merges or overwrites unmanaged settings. Empty/missing directories receive fixed settings and marker as BOM-less UTF-8. File/permission failures map to the profile error. Re-running setup is idempotent for a valid managed profile, not a repair operation for tampering.

blocks.title: Reject personal-profile ancestors and filesystem redirection
blocks.explanation: Paths must be nonblank and absolute, are normalized, then every ancestor is checked. Any directory named .copilot or an existing reparse-point ancestor fails, avoiding accidental adoption of the personal default profile or redirected ownership root. This is a point-in-time check; nonexistent ancestors are not resolved against future mutations.

blocks.title: Allow only known profile inventory and empty customization folders
blocks.explanation: The exact bounded marker is required. Top-level entries are capped at 32 and cannot be reparse points. installed-plugins/skills/agents/hooks are allowed only when empty; session-state/logs/AppData may exist. Files are restricted to the marker, settings/config and SQLite session-store sidecars. Allowed storage directories are not recursively audited here, and their presence means hosted CLI local retention remains a boundary.

blocks.title: Validate settings semantically without accepting unknown behavior
blocks.explanation: Settings are bounded and parsed, duplicate property names fail, disableAllHooks must be true, and six other booleans must be false. ide and customAgents each have exactly one expected boolean. Exactly nine unique allowed properties are required, so missing or extra settings cannot pass by default. Equivalent whitespace/property ordering remains acceptable.

blocks.title: Permit narrow authentication metadata but no arbitrary configuration
blocks.explanation: Optional config.json is bounded at 65536 bytes with depth 16 and comment skipping. Only firstLaunchAt, user/account metadata and copilot_tokens keys are accepted; their values are not interpreted or emitted here. RequireOnlyBoolean enforces the exact nested shape for safety settings. I/O, malformed JSON, bad shapes and decoding errors collapse to the fixed profile message.

blocks.title: Bound both bytes and decoded characters in profile reads
blocks.explanation: ReadBounded opens with read/write sharing, checks stream byte length, then reads at most limit+1 characters with strict UTF-8 and rejects a character overflow. This limits allocation and malformed text while tolerating another reader/writer; it is not an atomic directory snapshot. The final error asks for explicit setup/sign-in but does not perform either action.

files.role: Parses a bounded one-shot CLI event stream without confusing reasoning, metadata, final-message echoes or incomplete process exit with an answer.

blocks.title: Declare independent framing, stream and answer budgets
blocks.explanation: The assembly exposes internals to the test project. Limits are 262144 decoded characters per record, 2097152 total, 8192 records and 32768 answer characters. These are character limits, not byte or token limits. Separate message/turn IDs and terminal flags prevent repeated final output from looking like new deltas.

blocks.title: Reject errors and tools before considering content
blocks.explanation: JSON depth is limited to 32 and every record needs a string type. Nothing is accepted after result. Tool-shaped event types fail immediately; errors/retries/aborts fail rather than triggering a provider retry. A result needs integer exitCode zero, ended message/turn, idle and nonempty accumulated text. Other events require object data. The final process exit is checked separately.

blocks.title: Correlate streamed text to one turn and one message
blocks.explanation: A second turn, model start or message start is rejected. Message start requires a turn; model-call start is tracked but is not a mandatory prerequisite for message text in this parser. Deltas must match messageId and precede finalization, are bounded before append, and empty deltas produce no event. Sequence numbers for the app are added by the provider, not read from these records.

blocks.title: Treat the final message as validation, not duplicate answer text
blocks.explanation: Any nonempty/malformed toolRequests field fails before its associated content can be returned. A single final message without prior deltas can supply the answer; otherwise its content must exactly match accumulated deltas. Then matching turn_end and a single idle must occur in order. The parser never silently overwrites already streamed text with a different final answer.

blocks.title: Check known customization and model-outcome records
blocks.explanation: Only disabled builtin github-mcp-server/githubiq descriptors are accepted, with no non-null plugin origin and no non-builtin source. Skills must report builtin provenance. model_retry and failed model outcomes fail; a reported file-edit request must be explicitly false. These are checks on observed event metadata, not proof that an external executable could never perform unreported work.

blocks.title: Ignore known non-answer records and require terminal process success
blocks.explanation: Usage checkpoints get special tool-surface validation. Session metadata, reasoning and usage are intentionally not returned as answer text; unknown types fail closed. Structural parse errors become a safe protocol message. Complete requires both real exit zero and a previously verified result. MatchMessage centralizes exact correlation, preventing foreign deltas from entering the buffer.

blocks.title: Reject nonzero advertised tool usage and plugin origin
blocks.explanation: If promptCacheBreakState exists, every reported model's optional tool_count/tool_tokens must be integer zero, tools an empty array and tools_truncated numeric zero. Missing checkpoint fields are not treated as mandatory wire evidence. HasPluginOrigin rejects any non-null sourcePlugin/version/name metadata on an MCP descriptor. Malformed checkpoint shapes are caught by Accept.

blocks.title: Bound append and require explicit string types
blocks.explanation: Append compares new length against remaining capacity, avoiding overflow-prone addition. RequiredString distinguishes absent/non-string data from allowed empty strings. ReadRecordsAsync accepts configurable total/record limits so persistent ACP can reuse framing with a larger lifetime budget; each invocation starts fresh counters and a 4096-character read buffer.

blocks.title: Reassemble fragments without accepting truncated final records
blocks.explanation: Every read contributes to total decoded output before per-character parsing. Newline ends a record, counts even empty lines, and removes a single preceding CR. Empty lines are rejected by default or skipped for ACP. A pending record cannot exceed its cap even if the process never prints a newline. EOF with pending characters is incomplete; decoding failure is protocol failure, not replacement text.

blocks.title: Expose bounded safe failure categories
blocks.explanation: Factories provide stable protocol, output-limit, tools/customization and provider-failure codes with fixed messages. They do not incorporate raw JSON, stderr, question text or model output. Callers can show actionable status while retaining already accepted answer text as incomplete.

files.role: Owns one launched child and its cleanup, drains bounded stderr concurrently and carries only safe process-failure information.

blocks.title: Track bounded error state rather than retaining raw stderr
blocks.explanation: The process, linked cancellation, drain task and optional Windows Job handle are per-instance. stderr is capped at 65536 decoded characters. An optional inspector can classify Agency authentication text; only a safe exception and overflow flag are retained. Volatile/interlocked access later makes the background drain's result visible to the consumer.

blocks.title: Establish kill-on-close ownership and fail if assignment fails
blocks.explanation: Cancellation is checked before allocation and again before launch. On Windows a Job is configured with flag 0x2000, then the process starts and is assigned. Assignment failure kills/reaps the launched child and releases resources instead of continuing unowned. Assignment occurs after Process.Start, so this is lifecycle ownership, not a suspended-start sandbox. Successful construction registers kill-on-cancel and starts stderr draining.

blocks.title: Drain stderr concurrently and cancel on classified or excessive output
blocks.explanation: Reading stderr in 2048-character chunks prevents its pipe filling while stdout is consumed. The inspector runs before the size check; its first safe failure wins atomically. A failure, overflow or I/O/decoding problem cancels stopped, invoking owned-process cleanup. Expected cancellation of the drain is swallowed. Raw stderr is not accumulated for user-facing error strings.

blocks.title: Prefer known safe failures and delimit one-shot prompts with EOF
blocks.explanation: CheckErrorLimit first throws a classified failure, then the generic output-limit error. SendAsync writes exact prompt characters, flushes, and closes stdin rather than placing text in arguments or temporary prompt files. Pipe/encoding failures recheck stderr and caller cancellation before returning copilot_stdin. ACP bypasses this EOF-closing helper and writes its own persistent RPC stream.

blocks.title: Wait for exit plus stderr and kill only owned identities
blocks.explanation: WaitAsync awaits the direct child's exit, closes the Job to terminate surviving descendants, then waits for stderr drain and checks its outcome before exposing ExitCode. Kill targets the Process instance's tree and Job, never every process with a matching name. Expected race/platform errors in best-effort kill are suppressed.

blocks.title: Bound asynchronous cleanup while always releasing handles
blocks.explanation: Disposal cancels stopped and closes the Job, then separately allows up to five seconds for process exit and five for stderr completion. A timeout is a visible copilot_cleanup failure. The finally releases the cancellation registration, process and token source regardless. This is bounded cleanup, not a secure erasure guarantee for OS or external-provider state.

blocks.title: Match native Job structures and handle lifetime
blocks.explanation: Sequential structs provide the native basic and extended Job limit layout, including pointer-sized memory/affinity fields and I/O counters even though only the kill-on-close flag is set. SafeFileHandle owns the native Job. P/Invoke declarations preserve Win32 error state and marshal Boolean results so failed creation/configuration/assignment can fail startup safely.

files.role: Checks fixed prompt structure, literal-data preservation and mode-specific follow-up policy without invoking a model.

blocks.title: Round-trip default/null prompts through JSON
blocks.explanation: Fixtures include clear/noisy problem wording, injected JSON-looking text, attachment/command syntax, spacing and Unicode. Tests require the fixed policy prefix, exactly one decoded userQuestion field, and no literal newline/CR/@ in the serialized data. Both omitted and explicit null clarification must equal the string overload. These assertions prove envelope identity, not model resistance to hostile content.

blocks.title: Assert exact top-level task selection for all opted-in stages
blocks.explanation: Initial, correction and confirmed cases use hostile-looking current text and explicit synthetic history. Property lists must be exactly userQuestion/task/history and mode/instruction; the chosen instruction comes from the stage, not embedded JSON text. Initial gets empty history. This catches accidental default-history inclusion or arbitrary task fields before any transport is involved.

blocks.title: Preserve history fields without adding request identity
blocks.explanation: Every decoded history element must contain exactly userText and interpretation and equal the original strings. Encoded data must have no raw newline/CR/@. Changing RequestId must leave the prompt identical and its old GUID absent, showing correlation metadata is local transport state rather than model context.

blocks.title: Keep the agent-body policy aligned with clarification
blocks.explanation: Assertions inspect AgentDefinition itself, not merely a user prompt: it ends with the policy, includes tools: [], both task modes and the no-capability-escalation language. Stage instructions retain their explicit-action semantics. The UTF-8 byte-size assertion protects the 4096-byte profile validation bound. This verifies authored role content; actual placement in an external model's SYSTEM message is measured separately by acp_probe.py.

blocks.title: Reject invalid context and avoid prompt overfitting
blocks.explanation: Malformed UTF-16 and a fully consumed history budget fail before serialization with specific codes. Policy checks require runnable C#, complexity and direct-answer defaults while excluding the benchmark problem name, noisy phrase and workspace command. A separate direct-input Unicode case requires agency_question. These structural tests cannot establish generated code correctness or successful ASR interpretation.

blocks.title: Positive and negative controls for the nonanswer heuristic
blocks.explanation: The theory labels direct requests for a problem, a clarification footer and a final clarification line as nonanswers. Assumption-based solutions, explanatory quotations, ordinary prose and code-fenced prompt strings are negative controls. This tests the listed lexical patterns and fence handling, not exhaustive semantic detection or all Markdown nesting forms.

files.role: Exercises the production Agency lifecycle against scripted PowerShell ACP peers, including configuration, cancellation, ownership and clarification failures; no real model is part of this fixture.

blocks.title: Transport warmup has no conversation or question
blocks.explanation: Each fixture owns a unique test root and counts transformed launches/version checks. On Windows, two transport warmups must emit only initialize and launch only version plus engine. The first request adds new/select/prompt/close; Stop empties the request root. This establishes the scripted protocol sequence, not absence of unobservable work inside a real Agency installation.

blocks.title: Separate configuration lookup from prepared-session readiness
blocks.explanation: EffectiveModel cases verify default and explicit choices without any launch. The warmup test expects initialize/new/set_config_option but no prompt, repeats warmup idempotently and checks owned cleanup after Stop. Non-Windows process cases return without execution rather than proving portability; EffectiveModel itself remains a non-process test.

blocks.title: Reuse the engine but never reuse question sessions
blocks.explanation: Two public-safe clear/noisy strings are sent through the same provider. Each receives exactly two deltas plus Completed with request-local IDs and sequences 1,2,3. Captured questions must equal their originals and have different session IDs, while launch/version counts remain two/one. The fake returns a fixed answer, so this proves payload and lifecycle, not that a model understands either wording.

blocks.title: Automatic preparation adds an empty session only
blocks.explanation: With prepareNext enabled, explicit WarmUpAsync synchronizes with background preparation. After each answer, new-session count exceeds prompt count by one. Stop freezes the method log and leaves no owned workspace after a brief wait. The delay samples post-stop behavior; it is not a proof over every possible concurrent schedule.

blocks.title: Keep attachment and command-looking syntax literal
blocks.explanation: Inputs beginning with /help or @ paths, and multiline shell/delegation syntax, are recovered from the fake server's parsed JSON exactly. literalAt must be false in the transmitted prompt. This proves the production envelope reaching the scripted peer, not the full external CLI's treatment of every possible escape sequence.

blocks.title: Clarification history is explicit and disappears for independent requests
blocks.explanation: Initial interpretation, correction, confirmation and a normal request share one engine but use distinct sessions. Each capture is structurally compared to AgencyAnswerPrompt's expected JSON, must contain one text prompt and no literal @, and must close once. The final normal request has no implicit earlier context. This transport test uses fixed synthetic interpretations; it does not simulate human approval.

blocks.title: Permit follow-up prose only for interpretation metadata
blocks.explanation: Three nonanswer shapes are crossed with default, interpret and confirmed stages. Interpretation accepts the text and closes normally; default/confirmed require agency_nonanswer, no session/close method and complete engine-directory cleanup. Every case sends exactly one prompt. Partial deltas may have been delivered before terminal rejection; the test collects them indirectly rather than checking UI labelling.

blocks.title: The interpretation exception does not weaken ACP safety
blocks.explanation: Permission/input requests, tools, plans, missing notices, bad/missing terminals, empty/oversized answers, close failure and agent changes are injected while Confirmed is false. Exact failure codes and cleaned request directories are required. One prompt is counted in each case. These cases isolate transport invariants from the prose-only follow-up exception.

blocks.title: Reject clarification before launch or workspace creation
blocks.explanation: Null, blank, malformed-surrogate and 8193-character current text, plus a full history with no room for Yes, must yield clarification-specific errors. Launch count and method log stay empty, and the requests directory does not exist. The fixture's own sentinel/root setup is separate from provider side effects, so the assertion is not that the entire test performed no I/O.

blocks.title: Observe first-text timing once without body content
blocks.explanation: StageObserver records event, request ID, elapsed milliseconds and code for one synthetic request. FirstAnswerText appears once, every stage is associated with the request and fixed codes omit the sentinel word. Submission and close-completion markers are required. The 30-second range is a fixture bound, not a latency SLO or a test of the entire diagnostics persistence subsystem.

blocks.title: Enumerate configuration and protocol rejection paths
blocks.explanation: The table covers reverse RPCs, plan/tool updates, wrong session/response identities, malformed ID type, notices/terminal failures, model/effort/agent drift, allow-all, engine mismatch, nonanswers, output overflow and authentication. Each must return its safe code, omit private error text and clean the owned tree. Early model/config/engine failures additionally must never reach session/prompt.

blocks.title: Cancel or abandon after one delta without preserving the engine
blocks.explanation: A delayed prompt yields Synthetic before cancellation or iterator disposal. Cancellation must throw; both paths remove the owned workspace. After abandonment a later warmup creates another engine but reuses the unchanged wrapper-version stamp, reflected in one version check and three total launches. These cases test iterator cleanup through the real process wrapper, not real-model cancellation acknowledgement.

blocks.title: Stop during readiness and distinguish the answer deadline
blocks.explanation: Delayed initialize/new-session scripts let the test wait for an observed method before calling StopAsync. Warmup must cancel without a prompt and clean its tree. A separate four-second deadline during a delayed answer must return agency_timeout. Poll loops and deadlines keep these synthetic process tests bounded but remain scheduling-sensitive observations.

blocks.title: Invalidate version metadata and reject reused session IDs
blocks.explanation: Stopping/restarting with an unchanged sentinel executable reuses the version result; appending bytes forces another verification. A fake third session reuses the first ID and must fail before sending the third prompt. These tests prove length/stamp invalidation and per-engine session identity tracking, not cryptographic executable trust or globally unique IDs across engine rotation.

blocks.title: Refuse warm-profile customization injection
blocks.explanation: After preparation, the test adds an unapproved skill, alters the controlled agent body or creates another agent. The next request must fail agency_profile before any prompt and remove its owned state. These selected point-in-time mutations exercise known discovery paths; they do not cover all filesystem races, reparse permutations or opaque engine caches.

blocks.title: Rotate after 32 sessions and stop unsupported wrappers before ACP
blocks.explanation: Thirty-three successful questions require 33 new/close pairs and a second engine but only one unchanged wrapper-version check. Explicit disposal empties the tree. An unsupported wrapper string must cause agency_version after one version launch with no ACP method log. The tests rely on the transformer, not a real installed wrapper.

blocks.title: Assert no-side-effect guards and the exact launch surface
blocks.explanation: Pre-cancelled/empty requests perform zero launches; disposed providers reject both warmup APIs. A separate ProcessStartInfo inspection requires hidden redirected shell-free launch, exact default model/low effort and all candidate flags, including nonempty sentinel and deny-read. Prompt, plugin/MCP injection, allow-all/yolo and login arguments are forbidden. Inspecting flags does not prove how every CLI version interprets them.

blocks.title: Check environment stripping and the cosmetic settings exception
blocks.explanation: Synthetic credentials, routing/proxy settings and discovery variables are removed, but Agency's real-style APPDATA/LOCALAPPDATA values remain. Generated settings accept only a cosmetic announcement addition; changing disableAllHooks or adding hooks fails, as do array/malformed JSON shapes. These are configuration-function tests, not monitoring of real authentication storage or network traffic.

blocks.title: Reject unsafe resolution and implicit provider crossover
blocks.explanation: Relative executables, shell strings, missing .exe and .cmd paths fail resolution with agency_not_found. A Copilot-mode settings object cannot construct Agency, and Agency cannot carry a loopback endpoint. No installed binary is required for these negative checks, and no fallback provider is selected.

blocks.title: Replace launches with a deterministic fake peer, not Agency
blocks.explanation: CreateProvider writes a nonexecutable sentinel, then the internal transformer counts launches, verifies generated TOML/agent content and substitutes Windows PowerShell. Version output is synthesized; engine output comes from FakeServer with a chosen scenario and escaped capture directory. prepareNext defaults false for deterministic assertions. Helpers read the method log and drain the real provider iterator. Thus transport/lifecycle logic is real, but binary/model qualification is not.

blocks.title: Fake ACP initialize and session configuration are executable test logic
blocks.explanation: Emit writes compact flushed NDJSON; Chunk wraps agent_message_chunk with current session identity. The loop parses each request and records its method. initialize advertises the required close capability or a bad version; delayed scenarios sleep. session/new generates IDs and all five option values, with switches for replayed IDs, wrong model/effort, allow-all and missing agent advertisement. Those variations drive early rejection assertions.

blocks.title: Fake agent selection, prompt capture and forbidden capabilities
blocks.explanation: The fake verifies the requested agent config ID/value, optionally fails selection, and emits both an update and result. Prompt handling checks session identity, parses the envelope's final JSON line, and records exact question/history plus literalAt/prompt count. Authentication writes only synthetic private detail to stderr; reverse permission/input RPCs and tool/plan updates deliberately violate the client boundary. Valid scenarios then emit both configuration notices.

blocks.title: Fake nonanswers, configuration drift and terminal corruption
blocks.explanation: Branches emit leading refusals, a direct clarification or a long code-fenced answer with a clarification footer to exercise terminal prose scanning. Agent-changed emits invalid full configuration mid-prompt. Other branches change session ID, exceed answer capacity, omit text, pause after one delta, end the process without terminal, or return max_tokens instead of end_turn. The normal path produces two fixed chunks, not inferred text.

blocks.title: Fake close and response-identity failures remain observable
blocks.explanation: close-failure emits a matching RPC error with synthetic private text. Otherwise the peer echoes the active numeric ID, except wrong-response and wrong-id-type scenarios. Unknown methods terminate the script. The class Dispose recursively removes its test root after provider disposal by individual tests. This final script block is essential negative-control logic, not disposable fixture boilerplate.

files.role: Replays sanitized one-shot Agency event shapes and checks startup/authentication/tool-usage parsing independently of ACP process execution.

blocks.title: Define a sanitized terminal-complete one-shot replay
blocks.explanation: The fixture explicitly replaces IDs/model keys and excludes account metadata, system segments and cache fingerprints. It includes disabled builtin MCPs, one turn/model/message, two deltas, matching final content, zero-tool usage, idle and result. This encodes an expected event shape; it is not raw generated evidence and does not describe persistent ACP messages.

blocks.title: Distinguish opt-in receipt replay from the committed synthetic replay
blocks.explanation: An environment-selected receipt is read only when explicitly configured, byte-bounded, required to contain 17 records and to yield PHANTOM_OK without launching anything. The always-available replay adds accepted startup banners and verifies only two deltas, no duplicated final text, success on exit zero and failure on nonzero exit. Absent opt-in returns silently; that is not evidence an external receipt passed.

blocks.title: Startup chatter cannot mask arbitrary output or post-JSON errors
blocks.explanation: Negative durations, seven digits, trailing text and arbitrary notices fail the strict preamble adapter. A startup banner after JSON and a duplicate resolving banner also fail. These checks preserve the event boundary rather than treating human-readable wrapper output as trusted answer text.

blocks.title: Inspect reported tool metadata and malformed checkpoint structures
blocks.explanation: Synthetic usage records vary one tool-related field at a time: nonzero count/tokens, nonempty tools and Boolean/nonzero truncated counts all fail copilot_tools. Object/null/missing nested checkpoint shapes fail safely. These tests assert rejection of observed metadata; they cannot detect tool work that an external process does not report.

blocks.title: Detect stderr marker fragments without rejecting JSON question text
blocks.explanation: Each authentication phrase is split after three characters so a fresh guard must retain enough prior text to recognize the second fragment. Safe errors must omit the appended private sentinel. A user.message JSON record asking about sign-in remains ordinary metadata, preventing broad string matching over all prompt content. This validates the listed phrases, not every possible authentication flow.

files.role: Checks immutable history, stage limits, aggregate/per-field budgets and Unicode rejection without launching providers.

blocks.title: Mutate the caller's list after construction as a negative control
blocks.explanation: The original list is replaced and cleared after AnswerClarification copies it. Assertions require equal retained content, a different turn object, read-only list exposure and throwing mutation APIs. ValidateFor accepts an untrimmed correction. This proves defensive collection copying and string preservation, not a thread-safe mutable conversation manager.

blocks.title: Cover the exact interpretation-versus-confirmation stage matrix
blocks.explanation: Unconfirmed requests with zero through three completed turns validate; confirmed requests accept one through four. Confirmation without history, interpretation after four turns and any fifth stored turn fail distinct stage/round/history codes. The test calls constructors directly; actual explicit user consent is owned by MainWindow.Clarification, not inferred here.

blocks.title: Bound lazy enumeration and reject absent history
blocks.explanation: A deliberately endless iterator throws if a sixth item is requested. Construction must reject on the fifth yield with clarification_history_limit, proving it does not eagerly materialize arbitrary input. Null history and a null element get safe history errors. It cannot stop an enumerable whose MoveNext itself blocks indefinitely; that is outside these synchronous checks.

blocks.title: Apply nonblank and 8192-unit validation to every field
blocks.explanation: Null/empty/whitespace inputs are tested as user history, interpretation history and current text. Exactly 8192 ASCII units are accepted in a three-field combination; adding one unit fails independently in each position. Values are rejected rather than clipped. This is per-field validation in addition to the separate aggregate bound.

blocks.title: Make the aggregate bound inclusive and reserve room for a reply
blocks.explanation: Two history turns total 24576 units and accept an 8192-unit current question exactly at 32768. One extra history unit makes the same current text fail. A history of exactly 32768 can be constructed for confirmation but cannot accept even Y; adding another turn fails in construction. The UI's separate result validation reserves room for Yes before accepting an interpretation.

blocks.title: Count UTF-16 units but require well-formed Unicode
blocks.explanation: 4096 emoji consume 8192 C# string units and are preserved despite larger UTF-8 byte size; one extra emoji exceeds the field limit. Lone/misordered surrogate cases are tried in all three text positions and must return clarification_unicode. A private-sentinel case verifies safe failure messages through the shared assertion helper.

blocks.title: Keep fixture generation and safe-code assertions explicit
blocks.explanation: Turns supplies short deterministic user/interpretation pairs. AssertCode requires AnswerProviderException, the specific code and no private sentinel in its message. These helpers avoid replacing semantic validation with generic exception assertions, but they do not execute any provider or inspect generated model wording.

files.role: Verifies invalid configuration is explicit and missing configuration selects no-send snapshot mode.

blocks.title: Reject null, unknown, integer and unmapped settings
blocks.explanation: Each case writes a unique temporary JSON file and asserts the precise exception type from LoadFromFile: null is invalid data; unsupported enum, integer enum and unexpected member are JSON errors. Finally removes the file. This tests parsing policy without loading the user's actual answers.json or starting a provider.

blocks.title: Prove missing-file default and oversized-file rejection separately
blocks.explanation: The test first loads a nonexistent random path and checks SnapshotOnly, then writes 8193 ASCII spaces and requires the byte-size guard to reject it. Cleanup always runs. The name NeverSend refers to the selected mode; this unit test does not observe a network stack or the application's later event handlers.

files.role: Tests request minimization, per-run clarification identity, terminal state and provider-setting boundaries in memory.

blocks.title: Freeze a synthetic draft and inspect the request surface
blocks.explanation: Create builds a real QuestionDraft snapshot with a synthetic provider label. The test requires exact snapshot text, a nonempty request GUID, null clarification by default and exactly three reflected request properties. This guards against accidentally serializing SourceRefs/provenance through an expanded request contract.

blocks.title: Separate current reply, stored exchange and original snapshot
blocks.explanation: After run construction the source history is cleared and draft edited; the run must keep its original snapshot, whitespace/Unicode correction and copied history. A new ordinary run must still have null clarification. A Yes snapshot with Confirmed metadata remains Yes as ExactText while the interpretation stays in history; this is request representation, not proof of a UI click.

blocks.title: Validate before constructing and finalize only with terminal evidence
blocks.explanation: Over-budget history/current text and malformed current Unicode fail when creating an opted-in run. Separately, a Hello delta is immediately readable while the state remains Streaming; Complete throws until an empty Completed event arrives. This proves two-phase application finalization, not that a provider's Completed event was honestly generated.

blocks.title: Ignore foreign/late callbacks but reject active protocol corruption
blocks.explanation: A foreign request cannot append; after cancellation, late matching text is ignored and Complete does not revive the run. During an active stream, duplicate sequence and post-terminal text throw. These tests distinguish lifecycle-stale events from corrupt events belonging to the current still-streaming request.

blocks.title: Retain accepted text on overflow and reject empty completion
blocks.explanation: An exact-capacity delta is accepted; the next character throws before append. Fail leaves the 32768-unit prefix visible and marks Failed. A separate terminal-only run cannot become complete with an empty answer. Whitespace handling is implemented in AnswerRun.Complete but this test uses empty text specifically.

blocks.title: Reject alternate destinations and provider mixing
blocks.explanation: Endpoint negatives cover DNS localhost, abbreviated/integer loopback, attacker suffix, HTTPS, credentials, query/fragment and encoded path. Exact IPv4 and bracketed IPv6 HTTP loopback examples pass. Undefined mode, missing local model, hosted/local endpoint mixing, shell-like path and argument-like model fail. These tests validate URI/settings rules, not redirects, external CLI network behavior or explicit-port enforcement.

files.role: Checks raw default stdin versus opted-in envelopes through a synthetic one-shot CLI and real provider cleanup.

blocks.title: Arrange all request stages without a real local model
blocks.explanation: A unique root and launch counter support a transformer-backed LocalModel provider. Default, initial, correction and confirmed cases use whitespace, Unicode and command/JSON-looking synthetic strings. Confirmation sends Yes; other cases send raw input. The loopback address is a dead sentinel because PowerShell replaces the external CLI and does not make model requests.

blocks.title: Default is raw stdin; clarification is the fixed envelope
blocks.explanation: Every case must complete with synthetic text and the correct request ID. Default capture equals raw text and excludes policy. Opted-in capture equals AgencyAnswerPrompt.Create, contains no literal @, and decodes to exact current text/history count. Two launches mean version plus answer; the owned request tree is empty and unused hosted profile absent. No assertion establishes a controlled SYSTEM role for direct Copilot.

blocks.title: Opt-in metadata neither permits tools nor delays validation
blocks.explanation: Both interpretation and confirmation reject a synthetic tool request with copilot_tools and clean their tree. Invalid clarification is then tested with an explicitly nonexistent executable: clarification errors must occur first and no request/stdin files may appear. This verifies ordering independently of executable availability and avoids treating setup failure as successful input validation.

blocks.title: Inspect production launch flags before replacing the child
blocks.explanation: CreateProvider writes a nonexecutable sentinel and uses the internal transformer. Normal launches must contain the sentinel and deny-shell flags and no question-bearing arguments. It then substitutes noninteractive no-profile Windows PowerShell, with either an allowed synthetic version string or FakeCli. Therefore tests cover application launch assembly and process handling, not the actual CLI's flag interpretation.

blocks.title: Fake stdin capture and final-only event stream
blocks.explanation: The script reads all stdin as UTF-8, writes only synthetic captured text, then emits a turn/model start, one final assistant message, turn end, idle and result. A switch inserts a shell toolRequest in that final message so the parser must reject before exposing associated content. Read drains the provider stream; fixture Dispose removes the test root. No streaming-delta timing is exercised by this final-only peer.

files.role: Checks managed profile preservation, launch flags, environment isolation and executable selection without invoking Copilot.

blocks.title: Preserve unmanaged configuration instead of adopting it
blocks.explanation: A managed profile can initialize twice without changing settings and validates successfully. A nonempty unmanaged directory containing {} must throw and retain that exact file. The fixture owns its temporary root and deletes it later. These assertions distinguish idempotent setup from overwriting or silently repairing a personal profile.

blocks.title: Reject injected files, changed settings and populated plugins
blocks.explanation: Unexpected MCP/instruction/plugin/hook files each fail validation. Changing disableAllHooks to false fails; restoring settings is a positive control before adding a populated installed-plugins directory, which independently fails. The cases target discovery/configuration surfaces, not live plugin execution.

blocks.title: Reject discovery directories and personal/default profile paths
blocks.explanation: Nested synthetic skill content under .agents/.claude/.github/skills causes dedicated-profile rejection. The default .copilot path and a relative profile path also fail initialization. The checks prove these names/path forms are not adopted; no reparse-point race or every platform path spelling is exercised here.

blocks.title: Inspect the shell-free prompt-free launch contract
blocks.explanation: ProcessStartInfo must disable shell execution and visible windows, redirect all streams and include sentinel, deny-tool, instruction/MCP and remote-export restrictions. Allow-all/yolo/prompt switches are forbidden. This is structural validation of arguments, not proof that unsupported CLI builds honor them; version pinning and offline integration are separate layers.

blocks.title: Remove inherited secrets, routing and runtime injection
blocks.explanation: The test explicitly seeds many sensitive environment keys and a PATH containing relative entries around one absolute root. SanitizeEnvironment must remove all seeded overrides, leave only the absolute path, select COPILOT_HOME and disable OTEL. Synthetic strings are negative controls, not real credentials. The test does not launch or monitor a child.

blocks.title: Separate all direct-Copilot home/discovery roots
blocks.explanation: A synthetic inherited .agents skill is created, and every known home/config discovery variable points at that parent directory. Sanitization must redirect HOME/USERPROFILE/AppData/COPILOT_HOME and remove custom instructions, Claude and XDG keys so no environment value retains the parent path. This validates environment mapping, not a general filesystem-access restriction.

blocks.title: Require offline loopback routing without supplied credentials
blocks.explanation: LocalModel launch must carry offline=true, the configured loopback URL and OpenAI/completions selection, with no provider API key or GitHub token. There is no network call in this test, so it cannot prove no fallback or redirects in an arbitrary installed binary; the explicit installed-CLI fixture covers a narrower observed wire sample.

blocks.title: Accept an existing executable path as one filename, not a command
blocks.explanation: Relative, shell-shaped, missing and shell-wrapper paths fail. An existing .exe path containing spaces is accepted unchanged even though its synthetic contents are not executable, demonstrating resolution's limited responsibility. Dispose removes the test root. Binary identity and startup safety belong to subsequent provider/process checks.

files.role: Tests one-shot parser state, terminal requirements, metadata exclusion, safe failures and bounded fragmented record framing in memory.

blocks.title: Build valid prefixes and terminal suffixes explicitly
blocks.explanation: Event serializes type/data. Started emits one turn, model call and message start; End requires the final message to return no extra text, then sends matching turn_end, idle and result. Keeping these helpers visible makes later tests' ordering assumptions clear. They are fabricated protocol records, not evidence from an installed CLI.

blocks.title: Stream Unicode once and support a final-only answer
blocks.explanation: Deltas containing emoji and CRLF are returned immediately, but Complete fails until a matching final message and terminal suffix arrive. The final echo is not appended again. A separate no-delta case returns the final message once and completes normally. These are parser-level observations, not GUI rendering or byte-decoder tests.

blocks.title: Reject tools/errors and exclude reasoning/usage
blocks.explanation: Error, retry, tool and unknown event cases require exact safe codes and no raw private marker. A final message with toolRequests must fail before returning its content. Reasoning_delta and usage return null and cannot make an answer complete. This tests reported protocol content; unreported external process actions remain outside it.

blocks.title: Require both terminal evidence and actual exit; never rewrite deltas
