blocks.explanation: Even a complete event sequence cannot pass with process exit 1, and late events after result fail. Malformed JSON/shapes, premature results/turn-end and wrong message identity/type fail. A final content string different from the streamed prefix is rejected instead of overwriting visible output. No real process is launched to supply the exit code.

blocks.title: Bound text and restrict reported customizations
blocks.explanation: An exact 32768-character answer is accepted and one extra unit rejected. User skills fail while builtin skills pass. Disabled known MCP descriptors are accepted; connected/custom/user-origin/plugin-origin variants fail. These positive and negative controls document intentionally tolerated builtin metadata without treating all disabled server names as safe.

blocks.title: Reject model failures/edits and reconstruct one-character fragments
blocks.explanation: Native model outcome records must report success and no built-in file edit. Failure/result-error/edit=true cases are rejected. FragmentReader then returns one UTF-16 character at a time, splitting surrogate pairs and CRLF boundaries; ReadRecordsAsync must reproduce two complete records exactly. This validates character framing, not transport byte encoding.

blocks.title: Exercise record, record-count, aggregate and truncation ceilings
blocks.explanation: A 262145-character unterminated record and 8193 small records independently fail the limit. Repeated 1000-character lines exceed the aggregate budget; EOF after {} without newline is incomplete. The custom reader caps each read to fragmentSize. These deterministic memory tests do not establish real-process cleanup, which CopilotOwnedProcessTests covers separately.

files.role: Opt-in installed-CLI qualification against synthetic loopback HTTP/SSE peers, including no attachment expansion and redirect rejection.

blocks.title: Require an explicitly chosen installed binary and synthetic data
blocks.explanation: Without PHANTOMFUDGE_COPILOT_TEST_EXE the theory returns without exercising the CLI. Otherwise it creates a sentinel attachment file and plain/file/quoted-file/slash question cases, a loopback listener on an ephemeral port, a 30-second token and a terminal-release TaskCompletionSource. Unlike the fake-provider tests, this fixture starts an installed executable and a local network peer; it was not run during documentation.

blocks.title: Prove first text precedes terminal release and clean the owned tree
blocks.explanation: The real CLI is configured as LocalModel against the mock. The consumer must receive Synthetic before signalling finish, proving observable streaming rather than one final buffered return. Remaining events must concatenate to the Unicode answer, finish with Completed and carry increasing correlated sequences. The unused hosted profile must stay absent and request root empty. Finally releases any waiter, cancels/stops the mock and removes fixture files.

blocks.title: Set up redirect-origin and destination negative controls
blocks.explanation: The opt-in theory covers HTTP 301/302/303/307/308. Two independent loopback listeners separate the initially configured endpoint from the redirect target, so the test can observe forwarding rather than merely a failed response. A bounded token and provider deadline avoid waiting indefinitely. This setup covers the chosen CLI and local HTTP cases, not arbitrary external service policies.

blocks.title: Reject redirect answers and observe no pending retry/forward
blocks.explanation: Any yielded answer event fails the redirect test. The expected outcome is copilot_model_error, with neither destination nor origin showing a pending connection after server handling, no hosted profile and cleaned requests. Finally stops both listeners and deletes the root. Pending() is an observation at this point in a bounded run, not continuous packet capture or proof about all networking paths.

blocks.title: Serve either a redirect or a deliberately split SSE answer
blocks.explanation: RedirectAsync first reads the synthetic request, then sends Location plus zero-length body and connection close. ServeAsync checks the request, emits assistant role and first text, waits until the consumer acknowledges seeing it, then emits Unicode text, stop and [DONE]. That synchronization is the causal evidence for streaming; a mere elapsed timestamp would be weaker.

blocks.title: Bound raw HTTP headers/body and reject attachment expansion
blocks.explanation: The minimal fixture reader consumes bytes until CRLFCRLF under a 32768-byte cap, requires POST /v1/chat/completions and a single bounded Content-Length, then reads exactly that many bytes. The sentinel file's contents must not occur in the body. It is a controlled test server, not a general HTTP parser supporting chunked transfer or arbitrary clients.

blocks.title: Assert model, zero tool surface and one exact user suffix
blocks.explanation: Decoded JSON must select synthetic, omit tools or provide an empty array, contain exactly one user message and end that message with two newlines plus the exact question. This permits a CLI-added prefix; it is not equality of the entire model payload. WriteChunk emits UTF-8 SSE choices with explicit finish_reason, completing the fixture's wire contract.

files.role: Exercises redirected stdin, bounded output and owned Windows process-tree cancellation with synthetic PowerShell children.

blocks.title: Build a synthetic noninteractive PowerShell child
blocks.explanation: StartInfo uses the absolute Windows PowerShell executable with shell execution disabled, no visible window and redirected stdin/stdout/stderr. -NoProfile/-NoLogo/-NonInteractive reduce unrelated test-environment effects; the script is one ArgumentList item. These process tests are Windows-only and never invoke Copilot or a model.

blocks.title: Send prompt data through stdin and drain stderr concurrently
blocks.explanation: The synthetic script reads stdin to EOF and returns only its character count while also writing stderr. The quoted/ampersand-bearing string is passed through SendAsync, so it is data rather than PowerShell code. The test requires matching length and exit zero under a 15-second token. It checks length, not byte-for-byte round-trip content.

blocks.title: Capture specific parent/child IDs and cancel owned descendants
blocks.explanation: The fake parent launches a sleeping child, prints that PID and sleeps. The test reads the PID, cancels, disposes in finally, then checks both IDs are no longer running. The test name says only owned processes; its assertions verify owned termination, not survival of a separately launched unrelated control process.

blocks.title: Bound stderr without including its body in an error
blocks.explanation: A child continuously writes a synthetic private marker to stderr. WaitAsync must surface copilot_limit and the message must omit that marker. This exercises the background drain and cancellation-triggered cleanup, not a model/CLI-specific error protocol. A 15-second caller token bounds fixture failure.

blocks.title: Bound newline-free stdout and verify the captured PID exits
blocks.explanation: The child floods stdout without record separators, exercising the pending-record cap rather than record-count limits. The parser must throw copilot_limit, then explicit disposal must reap the recorded process. IsRunning checks a specific PID and treats a missing process as stopped. These are synthetic lifecycle observations, not a general OS sandbox test.

files.role: Builds the separately invoked latency harness against the production Core provider rather than a duplicated adapter.

blocks.title: Reference the production provider from a .NET 10 executable
blocks.explanation: The SDK-style project selects Exe and net10.0 and references PhantomFudge.Core directly. Thus Program.cs measurements can identify the actual provider assembly rather than a parallel implementation. This project declaration does not run a benchmark or authorize cloud access; command-line gates are in Program.cs. Shared repository build properties remain external to this small file.

files.role: Separates cold, transport-only and prepared-session timing for fixed public-safe questions, persisting provenance and explicit measurement limitations.

blocks.title: Require an explicit measurement mode and bounded model choices
blocks.explanation: Exactly two or three arguments select a known preparation/cloud/suite mode, output receipt path and optional allowlisted model. Invalid inputs print usage and return 2 before constructing a provider. Suite dispatch derives prepared/transport flags and chooses three candidate trials or six ordinary trials. No arbitrary prompt argument is accepted.

blocks.title: Measure empty-session preparation separately from Ask
blocks.explanation: The single-question path uses one fixed noisy public-safe string. Total timing starts before provider construction, and await using ensures provider disposal before the receipt is produced. Warmup duration is stored before starting the Ask timer. Prepare-only repeats warmup and marks that operation complete without entering the model-request branch; completed here does not mean an answer was generated.

blocks.title: Time first text and terminal while counting client attempts
blocks.explanation: attempts increments immediately before enumerating StreamAsync, not from a remote model-call receipt. First delta initializes firstMs once; Completed sets completion time. Provider failures are retained by code and cancellation gets a fixed label. Diagnostics are stopped in finally. Preparation failure can leave attempts zero; an attempt count is not an observed upstream inference/retry count.

blocks.title: Persist single-run context and limitations rather than a headline latency
blocks.explanation: The receipt records mode/model/low reasoning, optional fixed question, client submission count, warmup/repeated-preparation/Ask timing, total including disposal, completion/failure and synthetic answer. Its limitations explicitly exclude real transcription accuracy, percentiles and universal latency guarantees, and note opaque upstream retries. Output is written to an explicit path; success exit requires completion without failure, not a quality score.

blocks.title: Contrast cold, transport-ready and fully prepared first trials
blocks.explanation: The suite alternates two exact intended/noisy strings without normalizing them. One provider is reused. The first trial may do no preparation, transport-only warmup or full warmup; all later trials call full warmup to synchronize with a prepared fresh session. PreparationBeforeAsk is kept outside the Ask clock, and submitted increments before streaming. Those startup distinctions prevent warm performance from being presented as cold-start performance.

blocks.title: Measure provider text/close, then apply only a preliminary usefulness filter
blocks.explanation: First text and terminal are measured around production StreamAsync, not WPF painting. A successful stream is preliminarily useful only if it contains a C# fence, Dictionary and O(n), with selected clarification/workspace phrases absent. This lexical filter neither compiles code nor proves the algorithm, overflow correctness or intended-problem match. Exceptions remain trialFailure rather than disappearing from the data.

blocks.title: Retain failed/slow trials and stop after an explicit failure
blocks.explanation: Each row stores readiness state, exact question, preparation/first-text/closed-session/stream-cleanup times, completion, failure, preliminary usefulness, strict under-5000ms flag and answer. Persist runs after every row; a failed trial sets suite failure and stops further submissions. A final persist follows diagnostics shutdown, retaining partial progress if preparation or later work fails. False preliminary usefulness alone does not make the suite exit nonzero.

blocks.title: Bind receipts to the compiled provider assembly
blocks.explanation: PersistAsync records effective and configured model separately, low effort, startup category, exact question provenance and SHA-256 of the loaded AgencyCliAnswerProvider assembly. Counts, all trials, total time and failure accompany explicit limitations about synthetic cases and excluded preparation. Assembly identity helps compare runs but is not a source-tree hash, runtime dependency inventory or proof that generated answers are correct.

files.role: A separately authorized ACP qualification harness that can observe offline wire role/tool/history properties or collect narrow live synthetic measurements; it is not the production ACP validator.

blocks.title: Fix public-safe inputs and declare the probe's restricted flags
blocks.explanation: The docstring limits receipts and input scope. Two constant intended/noisy questions feed the harness. FLAGS select ACP, an explicit fast model/low effort and no-tools/customization/remote restrictions; AUTH lists observable authentication notices. Imported HTTP/thread/process utilities mean even offline mode starts real processes and loopback networking when authorized, not a pure static test.

blocks.title: Reuse authored C# policy rather than maintaining a second prompt
blocks.explanation: answer_policy reads AgencyAnswerPrompt.cs and extracts the specifically formatted raw-string Policy body, stripping eight indentation characters. envelope serializes exactly userQuestion with ASCII escapes and removes literal @. This is a formatting-sensitive source extraction, not a C# parser, and it only exercises the direct envelope, not clarification metadata. plain_content normalizes string versus text-block message representations for wire observations.

blocks.title: Launch a real child and pump both output channels
blocks.explanation: Client starts a hidden subprocess with supplied cwd/environment and redirected byte streams, records monotonic launch timing and spawns daemon readers. Each reader limits readline to 262145 bytes and posts data or EOF into a shared queue. The queue itself is unbounded; later consumer limits should not be described as hard producer-side memory backpressure.

blocks.title: Frame one RPC and apply probe-level timeout/output checks
blocks.explanation: call increments a numeric ID, writes one JSON line and flushes. It waits up to 120 seconds per call, treats stdout EOF as failure, and caps consumed line bytes and cumulative bytes across calls. stderr/startup text is screened for auth markers; only recognized stdout banners pass. Unlike production, banner sequencing/duplication is not tracked and limits are bytes rather than decoded characters.

blocks.title: Collect ACP text without pretending to be the production state machine
blocks.explanation: A matching result returns accumulated text and timings; RPC errors become code-only RuntimeErrors. Other records must be session/update; tool/plan kinds fail and text content must be text. Configuration notices are skipped by prefix, not required or fully validated. Other update kinds are only recorded, and session IDs/configuration are not comprehensively enforced here. Production AgencyAcpConnection is deliberately stricter.

blocks.title: Terminate the specific child and require explicit offline/cloud selection
blocks.explanation: close kills only the captured PID tree if still alive, waits, joins reader threads with deadlines and closes all streams. Arguments select an explicit offline engine or --allow-cloud, handshake/catalogue/controlled-agent mode, allowlisted model and one or two fixed questions. There is no ambient permission to invoke cloud inference merely because this source is present.

blocks.title: Construct disposable probe configuration and optional controlled agent
blocks.explanation: A GUID .local directory contains work/home/profile, minimal TOML and fixed safety settings. The initial settings dictionary is retained for later comparison. --controlled-agent writes an agent with tools: [] and the shared policy. The environment strips most inherited values but retains PATH without the production absolute/current-directory filtering; HOME/USERPROFILE/COPILOT_HOME are isolated. These are probe-specific choices, not identical production hardening.

blocks.title: Observe actual offline SYSTEM/user/history/tool payload fields
blocks.explanation: The local HTTP handler suppresses access logging, decodes the model request and records only tool count, user/assistant counts, envelope count, model, exact-question match and whether Policy appears in a SYSTEM message. It emits a fixed streamed answer plus stop/[DONE]. SYSTEM placement is observed at this external engine boundary, not established by fake ACP tests. The handler lacks general HTTP body limits and is a controlled synthetic peer.

blocks.title: Choose offline mock engine or real Agency wrapper explicitly
blocks.explanation: Offline mode starts a loopback HTTP server, redirects app-data roots and configures COPILOT_OFFLINE plus the mock endpoint. Cloud mode wraps the same flags in installed Agency profile-only restrictions. Controlled-agent selection and requested model are explicit command values. Initial receipt mode/counters/calls/failure are metadata; no provider version allowlist is enforced by this harness at this point.

blocks.title: Record handshake and profile effects rather than silently assuming them
blocks.explanation: initialize reports protocol/agent version and capabilities into the receipt with engine-ready time. ownedProfileCheck compares parsed settings and lists nonempty customization categories under known roots. These are recorded observations, not rejection gates; the controlled agent itself legitimately makes one category nonempty. No result JSON was read as part of this documentation task.

blocks.title: Create fresh sessions, select the role and observe model catalogue
blocks.explanation: Handshake-only skips sessions; catalogue-only creates and closes one without prompting. Every returned session ID must be new. Controlled-agent mode requires advertisement and sends set_config_option; selected option values and model/reasoning choices are recorded. Offline request count must remain unchanged during preparation, a causal check that this observed empty-session setup did not request a model response.

blocks.title: Submit fixed envelopes and check the observed no-history wire shape
blocks.explanation: The harness increments its client attempt count, sends one text envelope, records session/new, first-text, completion and launch-relative timings, then requires end_turn/nonempty answer and closes. Offline postconditions require exactly the chosen number of HTTP requests, zero tools, one user, zero assistant messages and one exact envelope; controlled-agent mode additionally requires SYSTEM policy. Live mode cannot inspect those wire properties here.

blocks.title: Clean disposable state and publish only a summarized receipt
blocks.explanation: Finally closes the child/server and retries owned-directory removal up to six times, recording cleanupFailure if still busy. Offline observations are appended, the explicit output directory is created and a formatted receipt printed/written. Return status depends on failure, not cleanupFailure alone. Cleanup exceptions before receipt writing can still escape; this harness is not a production recovery service.

files.role: Separately compiles operator-reviewed synthetic benchmark code and tests a narrow Two Sum contract; never part of production answer execution.

blocks.title: Require explicit reviewed-code acknowledgement and a chosen receipt
blocks.explanation: The docstring excludes automatic arbitrary-answer execution. argparse requires --reviewed-csharp, receipt and output paths, then reads trials and selects a unique .local workspace. The flag is an operator assertion, not a sandbox or automated proof of safe code. This tool invokes compilation/execution later and was not run for documentation.

blocks.title: Hash original snippets before adapting them for a shared harness
blocks.explanation: Each trial must have exactly one C# fenced block. Its original UTF-8 bytes are hashed before renaming the first public class to AnswerN and removing line-leading using directives. A generated Check call and original source hash retain provenance. These regex adaptations accept only a narrow source shape and can change compilation context; the hash is of the extracted original snippet, not the transformed executable.

blocks.title: Discover the exact callable C# signature
blocks.explanation: The embedded C# program supplies common imports and collects result objects. Reflection searches declared public static/instance methods for exactly one int[] return and (int[], int) parameters, otherwise adds a contract failure. Nonstatic classes are instantiated. Constructors and reviewed method code execute with ordinary process privileges; the harness does not contain arbitrary code.

blocks.title: Test duplicate indices, signs, zeros and overflow false pairs
blocks.explanation: Ten fixed arrays include normal pairs, duplicates, negative values and Int32 extremes designed to expose narrow arithmetic. Returned indices must be two distinct in-range positions and their mathematical sum is checked after widening the first operand to long. TargetInvocationException means that case fails. This validates cases, not all inputs, runtime complexity or ASR intent.

blocks.title: Define no-pair semantics and generate the temporary project
blocks.explanation: For [1,2] targeting 100, either an empty array or an ArgumentException is accepted; other behavior fails or can escape if not covered by the filtered catch. The CHECKS placeholder is replaced, then a net10.0 executable project and transformed classes are written under the owned workspace. The production provider never reaches this code-generation path.

blocks.title: Run bounded validation and preserve per-trial source provenance
blocks.explanation: dotnet run executes the reviewed harness with captured output and a 90-second timeout. Nonzero exit and timeout receive fixed failure labels; success parses the final stdout line as JSON checks. Finally deletes the temporary project. Output records hashes, compiled status, check outcomes and counts. Exit zero means compiled with no recorded failed checks, not a general proof of correctness or safe execution of arbitrary answers.

files.role: Historical one-shot Agency smoke harness with one explicit cloud consent flag and fixed marker prompt, retaining detailed receipts only locally.

blocks.title: Gate a fixed synthetic cloud smoke and build its profile
blocks.explanation: --allow-cloud is required before resolving the installed Agency path or creating a GUID LocalAppData probe tree. The only model input is a fixed marker request, not a caller-supplied meeting question. Minimal TOML and nine safety settings are written in owned work/profile paths. Unlike production ACP setup, this older harness does not create/select the controlled answer agent.

blocks.title: Launch the restricted one-shot wrapper, not persistent ACP
blocks.explanation: The environment keeps ordinary Windows values and real app-data roots, retains absolute PATH entries and isolates home/profile. The command disables wrapper plugins/MCP/AEC/input processing and uses the sentinel plus deny-read/shell/write/url, JSON streaming and no logging. It has no production wrapper/engine version verification and no ACP session lifecycle; it is a distinct historical probe surface.

blocks.title: Drain both pipes while sending only the fixed marker via stdin
blocks.explanation: Two daemon threads post bounded readline chunks and EOF to a queue, then stdin receives the fixed PHANTOM_OK instruction and closes. Separate collections retain records, event types, deltas and notices locally. Timing starts after launch and send, so seconds is not a cold-process startup measurement. The queue is unbounded despite later consumer-side output limits.

blocks.title: Enforce consumer byte/time limits and detect authentication notices
blocks.explanation: The loop waits for both channel EOF markers, checks a 120-second elapsed limit and caps cumulative bytes at 2MiB and each line at 262144 bytes. UTF-8 uses replacement decoding, unlike strict production readers, and strip normalizes surrounding whitespace. Auth markers in any decoded line stop the probe. These choices make this weaker than the production parser for exact malformed-output handling.

blocks.title: Collect deltas and reject selected reported capabilities
blocks.explanation: JSON stdout records are retained and type-inspected; tool event names, active MCP status or non-builtin skills cause failure. Only assistant.message_delta contributes output; final-message reconciliation and full terminal order are not implemented. Non-JSON text becomes notices. On failure the specific PID tree is killed, then the process is waited with a ten-second timeout. A matching marker alone is weaker than production terminal verification.

blocks.title: Keep detailed smoke receipts local and limit success semantics
blocks.explanation: Finally kills a still-running owned PID tree and closes output streams. Result includes failure, exit, event types, marker equality, character count, elapsed seconds and local receipt directory. Raw events/notices are written only to that LocalAppData tree and are not deleted here. Exit zero requires no recorded failure, exact trimmed marker and process exit zero; it does not establish controlled SYSTEM policy or benchmark quality.

files.role: Builds a separately invoked synthetic smoke tool against the same Core provider contracts as the app.

blocks.title: Use a small .NET 10 executable with a Core project reference
blocks.explanation: OutputType Exe and net10.0 define the console harness. The relative ProjectReference imports real AnswerConfiguration/providers rather than duplicating their implementation. This file contains no authentication, networking or launch action by itself; those actions require invoking Program.cs with its explicit synthetic/cloud gates.

files.role: Runs one manually authorized fixed-marker smoke through the configured provider, reporting only narrow completion/timing metadata.

blocks.title: Require synthetic invocation and explicit cloud consent
blocks.explanation: Only --synthetic-request with optional --allow-cloud is accepted. Settings are loaded normally; SnapshotOnly is rejected and either hosted mode requires cloud consent. A 120-second token and a new request GUID wrap the fixed PHANTOM_OK prompt. Agency uses its production adapter; other enabled modes use Copilot with the dedicated profile. The program does not accept arbitrary question text.

blocks.title: Require the marker and terminal while bounding displayed text
blocks.explanation: The timer starts immediately before enumeration; firstTextMs is set on the first delta and answer length is bounded again at the application limit. Completed is recorded separately and the final trimmed answer must equal PHANTOM_OK. This is a smoke test, not a useful technical-answer benchmark, semantic quality check or GUI-visible latency measurement.

blocks.title: Report narrow synthetic success and safe failure without retries
blocks.explanation: Success prints provider, first/total milliseconds, the known marker and synthetic/no-meeting-data flags. Selected setup/provider/I/O/cancellation exceptions become safe stderr and exit 1. The provider is held as IAnswerProvider without explicit asynchronous disposal; unlike AgencyLatencyProbe's await using, this entry point does not demonstrate graceful persistent-Agency shutdown or include it in totalMs. Normal process exit is not equivalent evidence.
